This workflowr site records the experiments behind the MoS-NMF project.
The current sequence starts from Poisson SuSiE, moves to matrix-factorization
Poisson SuSiE, and then studies the model-selection behavior that motivates
MoS-NMF.

## Main sequence

1. [Poisson SuSiE](1.poisson-susie.html): a single-observation sparse Poisson
   decomposition with posterior uncertainty over factor assignments.

2. [Joint learning of \(F\)](2.joint-learn-susie-poi-F.html):
   MF-Poisson-SuSiE when the shared factor matrix is learned rather than fixed.

3. [Overspecified \(D\)](3.overspecify-D-mf-poi-susie.html):
   how MF-Poisson-SuSiE behaves when the fitted number of single-effect
   dimensions is larger than the true support size.

4. [Overspecified \(K\)](4.overspecify-K-mf-poi-susie.html):
   how overfitting the factor dictionary creates redundant or competing factor
   rows, and how posterior assignment probabilities reveal that ambiguity.

5. [Tree scenario](5.tree-scenario.html): a harder no-anchor setting where every
   group uses multiple factors and support recovery depends on shared
   co-occurrence structure.

## Project question

The central question is whether posterior objects such as
\(\bar\gamma_{idk}\) and \(\bar\gamma_{sdk}\) can do more than recover sparse
supports: can they also diagnose model-selection uncertainty when \(K\), \(D\),
or later \(S\) is overfitted?
